For Loop Number Check

for_loop_nb_check.Rd

Check the sequence expression of every for loop of a function. If the number of iterations is not fixed by the writing itself (e.g., 1:length(x)), a checking line is added before the loop, issuing a warning at execution if the sequence is empty, contains NA or infinite values, has a single value, or is decreasing. Return a table-like message of the problematic lines and a corrected version of the submitted function.

Usage

for_loop_nb_check(
  x,
  export = FALSE,
  out_path = ".",
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

x

A function name, written without quotes and brackets.

export

Single logical value. Export the modified function into a .R file (see the out_path argument)? If TRUE, the file is named <function name>_safer.R (pkg::fun gives fun_safer.R) and contains <function name>_safer <- function(...) ..., so that base::source() recreates it. An error is returned if the file already exists, or if x is not a function name (inline definition like function(x){x}, or component like FUN_LIST$fun). Nothing is written if no modification is performed. See the @returns section for the returned value.

out_path

Single character string indicating the absolute pathway of the folder where to export the modified function when the export argument is TRUE. out_path = "." (default) means the R working directory set by the user. Ignored if the export argument is FALSE.

safer_check

Single logical value. Perform some "safer" checks? If TRUE, checkings are performed before main code running (see the safer-r project): 1) correct lib_path argument value 2) required functions and related packages effectively present in local R libraries and 3) R classical operators (like "<-") not overwritten by another package because of the R scope. Must be set to FALSE if this function is used inside another "safer" function to avoid pointless multiple checkings.

lib_path

Vector of characters specifying the absolute pathways of the directories containing the required packages for the function, if not in the default directories. Useful when R packages are not installed in the default directories because of lack of admin rights. More precisely, lib_path is passed through the new argument of .libPaths() so that the new library paths are unique(c(new, .Library.site, .Library)). Warning: .libPaths() is restored to the initial paths, after function execution. Ignored if NULL (default) or if the safer_check argument is FALSE: only the pathways specified by the current .libPaths() are used for package calling.

error_text

Single character string used to add information in error messages returned by the function, notably if the function is inside other functions, which is practical for debugging. Example: error_text = " INSIDE <PACKAGE_1>::<FUNCTION_1> INSIDE <PACKAGE_2>::<FUNCTION_2>.". If NULL, converted into "".

Value

A table-like text message indicating the for sequences not written with hard numbers, or a message saying that everything seems fine, printed by base::message().

Table-like: column 1, the line number in the function code (starting at the "<- function" line, i.e., without counting the #' header lines); column 2, the construct (for); column 3, the code preceding the construct body.

In addition:

If export = FALSE: the modified function (checking lines added, see the @details section), or NULL if no modification was performed (everything clean, or no checking line inserted).

If export = TRUE: NULL (invisibly), the modified function being written into the <function name>_safer.R file (see the export argument).

Details

Clean writings (not reported): hard numbers, i.e., an optional unary minus and a finite integer-valued numeric literal, optionally followed by : and another such literal, with nothing else (e.g., 3, -3, 1:3, 1e3, 1L:3L, 0x10:0x11), or a seq_len(...) or seq_along(...) call (namespaced or not) occupying the whole sequence expression. Any other writing is reported, e.g., variables (for(i in x), 1:n), calls (1:length(x), 1:nrow(df), base::rev(x = x)), arithmetic (1:(n - 1), 1:3 - 1, seq_along(x) - 1) and non-integer or non-finite literals (1:2.5, 1:NA, 1:Inf, 1:TRUE). Comments and strings are ignored. Rationale: x <- character() ; for(i in 1:length(x)){y <- i} loops twice and ends with y = 0, because 1:length(x) gives c(1, 0) when x is empty: base::seq_along(x = x) should be used instead.

Not reported either, because fully determined by the code itself (their control is the responsibility of the writer): the equal-bounds (0:0, 1:1), both-negative (-3:-1) and decreasing (1:0) hard-number writings.

Modification: each reported construct becomes tempo_for_seqN <- <SEQUENCE> ; <CHECKS> ; for(<VARIABLE> in tempo_for_seqN)<BODY> (N being the rank of the report), so that the checked sequence and the for controller are strictly identical. At execution, base::warning() is issued when the sequence is empty, contains NA or infinite values, has a single value, or is decreasing. Errors of the sequence evaluation itself (like 1:NA) are propagated as they are. Only the reported spans are modified: comments, strings and formatting are preserved elsewhere. A construct not preceded by a statement boundary (unbraced body of if/else/for/while/repeat, assignment value, function argument, operand, etc.) is wrapped in curly brackets. The returned function is in a new environment whose parent is the environment of the submitted function: check it before replacing the original one.

Warning: the checking lines are not inserted (the concerned constructs are listed in the message and remain unmodified) when:

  • the name tempo_for_seqN is already used in the function code (including comments and strings);

  • the reported construct is inside the sequence expression of another reported construct;

  • a construct requiring the curly bracket wrap contains comments (the wrap collapses it on a single line);

  • a construct requiring the wrap shares the end of its body with a later construct also requiring it (e.g., for(a in 1:n) for(b in 1:length(x)){...}).

Warning: with aliased bounds like n <- length(x) ; for(i in 1:n), only 1:n is analyzed (reported as a plain variable), not the origin of n.

Line numbers are indicative: compiled functions (like saferDev::colons_check) have no comments, hence line numbers different from their source file.

Examples

# Warning: these examples may not work well when using the "Run examples" link 
# because of a particular environment. Please, copy-paste in a local environment.
# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/for_loop_nb_check.html
fun1 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:3){ base::print(x = i) } }
saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun1)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun1(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
fun2 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun2)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun2(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
#> function (x) 
#> {
#>     tempo_for_seq1 <- 1:length(x)
#>     if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 0) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE EMPTY: 0 ITERATION", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::anyNA(x = tempo_for_seq1)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH NA VALUES", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) == 1) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH A SINGLE VALUE (EQUAL BOUNDS?): SINGLE ITERATION", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::any(base::is.infinite(x = tempo_for_seq1), 
#>         na.rm = TRUE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH INFINITE VALUES: NO ENDLESS LOOP POSSIBLE BECAUSE THE for() CONTROLLER IS FULLY EVALUATED BEFORE ITERATING, BUT CHECK THAT AN INFINITE VALUE IS EXPECTED", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::typeof(x = tempo_for_seq1) %in% 
#>         base::c("double", "integer") && base::all(x = tempo_for_seq1 < 
#>         0, na.rm = FALSE)) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE WITH ALL NEGATIVE VALUES", 
#>             call. = FALSE, immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, 
#>             domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     else if (base::is.atomic(x = tempo_for_seq1) && base::typeof(x = tempo_for_seq1) %in% 
#>         base::c("double", "integer", "character", "complex") && 
#>         base::length(x = tempo_for_seq1) >= 2 && tempo_for_seq1[1] > 
#>         tempo_for_seq1[2]) {
#>         base::warning("FOR SEQUENCE DECREASING", call. = FALSE, 
#>             immediate. = FALSE, noBreaks. = FALSE, domain = NULL)
#>     }
#>     for (i in tempo_for_seq1) {
#>         base::print(x = i)
#>     }
#> }
#> <environment: 0x564c124e8f70>
fun3 <- function(x){ for(i in base::seq_along(x = x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(fun3)
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun3(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
fun4 <- function(x){ for(i in 1:length(x)){ base::print(x = i) } } ; fun4_safer <- saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun4, export = FALSE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # modified function returned (checking line added)
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> INSIDE fun4(), SOME for() SEQUENCES ARE NOT WRITTEN WITH HARD NUMBERS:
#> 
#> LINE	CONSTRUCT		CODE
#> 3	for		for (i in 1:length(x)) {
#> 
#> MODIFIED FUNCTION RETURNED BY return().
#> 
fun5 <- function(x){ for(i in 0:0){ base::print(x = i) } } ; saferDev::for_loop_nb_check(x = fun5, export = FALSE, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "") # NULL returned: the degenerate hard-number writings are the responsibility of the writer, no checking line inserted
#> 
#> 
#> AFTER RUNNING saferDev::for_loop_nb_check().
#> INSIDE fun5(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN.
#> 
#> NULL
